title: When to Call Your Dentist After a Root Canal
metaTitle: When to Call Your Dentist After a Root Canal
metaDescription: The warning signs after a root canal that mean you should call your dentist — severe pain, swelling, fever, a lost filling, or bite problems.
secondaryKeywords: when to call dentist after root canal
excerpt: Most root canal recoveries are smooth, but a few symptoms deserve a prompt call. Here is how to tell the difference.
heroImageAlt: A phone resting on a table beside a glass of water, suggesting calling a dental office for advice.
bodyHtml:
Call your dentist after a root canal if you have pain that is severe or getting worse after the first few days, swelling of the gum or face, a fever, a lost or broken temporary filling, or a bite that feels wrong. Most recoveries are uneventful, and mild soreness for a few days is expected, but these particular signs are worth a prompt conversation rather than waiting to see if they pass.

What a normal recovery looks like

Before the warning signs, it helps to know what is ordinary. A treated tooth is often tender for two to three days, especially when biting, and the surrounding gum and jaw can feel a little sore. This usually eases steadily and responds to over-the-counter pain relief when your dentist has confirmed it is suitable for you. A recovery heading in the right direction feels a bit better each day.

Signs that warrant a call

Reach out to your dental office if you notice any of the following:

  • Pain that intensifies: discomfort that climbs after the first two to three days, becomes severe, or wakes you at night.
  • Swelling: a swollen gum, cheek, jaw, or face, particularly if it is spreading.
  • Fever or feeling unwell: a temperature or general illness alongside tooth symptoms can signal infection.
  • A lost or damaged temporary: if the temporary filling falls out, cracks, or feels very different, the tooth may be left unsealed.
  • Bite problems: if the tooth feels "high" or hits first when you close, it may need a small adjustment.
  • An allergic or medication reaction: rash, itching, or any reaction to a prescribed or over-the-counter medicine.

None of these automatically means something has gone wrong, but each is a reason to be assessed.

Signs that need urgent attention

Some symptoms should not wait for a routine callback. Difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling that is spreading quickly, swelling around the eye, or a high fever with significant facial swelling can indicate a serious spreading infection and warrant urgent or emergency care. These situations are uncommon after a routine root canal, but they are treated most safely when addressed early, so trust your instincts. When in doubt about severe or rapidly changing symptoms, seek help promptly rather than delaying, and do not assume you are overreacting by asking.

Why follow-up matters

A root canal is often completed in stages, and the tooth usually needs a permanent restoration such as a crown or filling to protect it. Leaving a tooth with only a temporary seal for a long time can allow bacteria back in. Keeping your follow-up appointment is one of the most reliable things you can do to support a good outcome, even if the tooth feels fine.

Should I take antibiotics if the tooth hurts again?

Antibiotics are not a do-it-yourself fix for tooth pain, and they do not replace needed dental treatment. If you think an infection is developing, contact your dentist, who can examine the tooth and decide whether antibiotics are appropriate in your situation.

Is it an emergency if my temporary filling comes out?

It is usually not an emergency, but it is a reason to call for advice soon so the tooth can be re-sealed. In the meantime, keep the area clean and avoid chewing on that side.

What should I have ready when I call?

It helps to note when your treatment was done, what symptoms you have, when they started, and whether they are improving or worsening. If you were prescribed anything or given written aftercare instructions, have those handy too. That makes it easier for the team to advise you and to decide whether you need to be seen.

Getting help when you need it

If you have had a root canal and something does not feel right, it is always reasonable to check in. For patients in the Markham area, you can contact Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham, where Dr. Neda Kadivar and the team provide root canal treatment and can advise on next steps. You can reach the office directly through the Smile Dental Arts Centre contact page.

This article is general information and not a substitute for professional dental advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always speak with a licensed dentist about your specific situation.
